chapter: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
title: How the Spirits picked up tunes from audiences
summary: The Spirits learned whatever the audience requested or they heard, being good enough to pick up tunes quickly.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Music brings it all back. When the Spirits -- how did the Spirits decide what tunes to play? Would people like make requests and you'd just decide you'd better learn them?
They'd come up, you know, and we'd be on stage and they'd come up and say, 'Can you play this, do you know this?' Or they'd holler out of the audience, 'Play so and so.' If we knew it we'd play it.
And more than likely we knew it.
So you'd just be learning new stuff all the time, as it came out.
Yeah. We'd hear it and we'd learn it. We'd get, just like you and I and Leroy's here now.

We'd get in a place like this with the group boys, trio, quartet, and every time we'd go in with someone we'd like to hear, we took him with us. As far as the musicianship was concerned, we knew that. But if we heard we took.
